kind.why: One job a harness runs, whose script starts or resumes the coding harness on a build folder and reads the folder's own check.

speed.limit: One harness run per message, up to the harness's own limit
speed.why: Each message moves the build to the person's next decision or to the end.

data.limit: Only the build folders it keeps, under its work folder
data.why: It writes nothing the plugin does not.

trust.limit: The person's approval passes through only on their own word

drivers.says: The harness and the plugin are the only authors of a build's files.
drivers.from: It is a harness, not a second author: it writes nothing the plugin does not.

drivers.says: Only the person's words are kept as theirs, so the check can find the words an answer quotes.

formats.convention: A short header with `build`, `phase` (spec, build or none) and `where` (where the build is, in the words of its own check), then `## What the build did` with what the harness said, then what the person may reply.

skills.name: build-an-agent
skills.responsibility: Takes the person's words and moves one build to the person's next decision or to the end.
skills.script: Starts or resumes the harness on a build folder, keeps the person's words in the folder's said.md before handing them on, passes the person's approval through only on their word, and reads the folder's check for the phase it is in.

parts.name: build keeper
parts.responsibility: Keeps each build's folder and harness session under its id.

parts.name: said keeper
parts.responsibility: Adds the person's message for a build to the folder's said.md under a heading with the time, and puts said.md back as it was when the harness cannot be run.

parts.name: harness runner
parts.responsibility: Runs the coding harness headless with the plugin, always with ADLC_NOT_THE_PERSON=1, and reads its answer.

parts.name: phase reader
parts.responsibility: Reads the build folder's own check for the phase it is in and what it still has missing, and says so in the check's words.

flow.says: The person sends a request, or an answer naming a build.
The harness runs the skill with the message, and the build keeper finds or starts the build.
An answer for a build is added to its said.md first.
The harness runner hands the coding harness the prompt in the build's session.
After the run, the phase reader reads the folder's own check.
The skill answers with where the build is, in the check's words, and the person's question.

decisions.decided: Drive the coding harness and never write a build's files
decisions.context: One builder writes an agent through the plugin; a second author here would be the separate-author line the plan retires.
decisions.why: The plugin's check holds what the harness writes; anything this agent wrote would be held by nothing.

alternatives.option: Write the spec and the files from the request itself
alternatives.why_not: It would be a second author outside the check.

consequences: Every file in a build comes from the harness through the plugin.

decisions.decided: Pass the person's approval through only when their message says approve for the build
decisions.context: The plugin keeps approval as the person's command, which the harness may not run.
decisions.why: With no person at the keyboard, the person's own word in their message is the approval.

alternatives.option: Let the harness approve when the check passes
alternatives.why_not: The approval would not be the person's.

consequences: A build waits in the spec phase until the person says approve.
The approval is offered in the reply only when the check says the spec waits for the person.

decisions.decided: Read the phase and what is missing from the build folder's own check, and say it in the check's words
decisions.context: The plugin works in two phases, the spec and the build, and its check names the phase and what each still needs.
decisions.why: The check is the judge of a build; a reply that judged for itself could say a build passed when it has not.

alternatives.option: Read the harness's own words for where the build is
alternatives.why_not: The harness can say it is done when the check does not.

consequences: The reply says the build has passed only when the check says so.
When the check does not answer, the reply says it could not tell.

decisions.decided: Once the spec is approved, ask the harness to carry on until the check says the build has passed
decisions.context: In the build phase the builder writes everything in any order and the check judges it together.
decisions.why: One run carries the build to its end or to something only the person can decide.

alternatives.option: Ask the harness for one stage at a time
alternatives.why_not: The build has no stages any more, only gates judged together.

consequences: A message after the approval usually ends with the build passed, or with the person's question.

decisions.decided: Keep the person's words in said.md itself, and run the harness with ADLC_NOT_THE_PERSON=1
decisions.context: The plugin keeps what is typed at the harness in said.md as the person's, unless the program typing says it is not the person.
decisions.why: The prompts this agent writes are not the person's, so the plugin must not keep them; the person's own answers are added by the agent before it hands them on.

alternatives.option: Let the plugin keep every prompt
alternatives.why_not: The agent's own prompts would read as the person's words.

consequences: An answer the builder writes for the person can be checked against what they really said.
When the harness cannot be run, said.md is put back as it was.
